newsitem.title: GERMANY: Debitel cuts rates on D1, D2 German mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Debitel cuts rates on D1, D2 German mobile phones.

text.p: Debitel, the mobile phone unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Metro AG, said on Thursday it would cut prices for private customers on Germany's D1 and D2 mobile phone networks.

From November 1 Debitel will cut monthly rentals and call charges for new customers, passing on price cuts announced in the past few days by D1 operator Deutsche Telekom AG and D2's Mannesmann Mobilfunk.
Separately, Germany's third mobile network E-plus said it would announce price cuts on Friday after earlier saying it saw no need for any reductions.
A spokesman for E-plus, owned by Veba, Thyssen, BellSouth and Vodafone, said he could not comment on the price cuts before an official announcement.

Debitel, a service provider which sells mobile phones to 750,000 German users and 200,000 in neighbouring countries, offers a range of deals aimed at high-volume business callers and those who see mobile phones as more of a handy accessory.
Rental charges for low-volume users will fall by between 43 and 50 percent, while call charges for active callers fall by 17.5 percent to 99 pfennigs per minute, it said in a statement.
